claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2, re-fetched RFC 6749 §1.1: "OAuth defines four roles"; authorization server "The server issuing access tokens to the client after successfully authenticating the resource owner and obtaining authorization"; resource server "The server hosting the protected resources, capable of accepting and responding to protected resource requests using access tokens"; client "An application making protected resource requests on behalf of the resource owner and with its authorization."

Round 2 text ("need not hold the password; in Đơn Hàng it never does") now matches RFC 6749 §1 (fetched): "the client obtains an access token" instead of sharing credentials; §1.3.3 password grant kept as the exception. Repo: keycloak/donhang-realm.json@stage-2 donhang-app "directAccessGrantsEnabled": false; live Keycloak rejects unknown flows for other clients too (see claim 13).

Round 3: s5 "The comment line right after `# lesson:` states its role:" checked against docker-compose.yml@stage-2:188-196 (git show): line 188 "# lesson: backend.l2.oauth2-roles", line 189 "# The authorization server: customers and staff type their passwords here," - the role is on that line. Round 2: donhang-realm.json "clientId": "donhang-app", "publicClient": true; Program.cs:37 "Keycloak issues the tokens; the api only checks them."

stage-2 DonHang.App/lib/screens/login_screen.dart:7 "From stage-2 there is no password here: the button leaves for Keycloak's ..."; git grep -i password in DonHang.App/lib finds no other field. keycloak_sign_in.dart: realmUrl = 'http://localhost:8180/realms/donhang'; start() calls goTo(authorizeUrl(...)). docker-compose.yml: KC_HOSTNAME "http://localhost:8180"; web service publishes "8180:8180" and proxies to Keycloak (Caddyfile :8180).

stage-1 DonHang.App/lib/api_client.dart:33-37 login() posts jsonEncode({'email': email, 'password': password}) to '$baseUrl/auth/login'. stage-1 AuthController [Route("api/v1/auth")], [HttpPost("login")]: PasswordHasher.Verify(request.Password, customer.PasswordHash), then tokenService.IssueToken(...).

Round 3: s5 "the file registers the client `donhang-app`... lists the accounts that can sign in, each with the same fake development password": donhang-realm.json@stage-2:18 "clientId": "donhang-app"; 6 users, all "enabled": true, each credentials {"type":"password","value":"donhang-dev-password"}. Round 2: git ls-tree stage-2 lacks AuthController/JwtTokenService/PasswordHasher; DropCustomerPasswordHash drops password_hash from customers.

Repo, not RFC (WebFetch of RFC 6749 did not return §7.1): stage-2 DonHang.App/lib/api_client.dart `'Authorization': 'Bearer $token'`; stage-1 api_client.dart `'Authorization': 'Bearer $_token'`; scripts/backend/auth-and-orders.sh@stage-2 `-H "Authorization: Bearer $token"` - the word Bearer, one space, the token; output@stage-2 shows the call succeeds with it.

tools/extract-code DonHang.Api/Program.cs --tag stage-2 --lines 34-45: `var authority = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Authority"] ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Keycloak:Authority is not set");` ... `options.Authority = authority;`. git grep -i SigningKey stage-2 -- DonHang.Api: no match (stage-1 Program.cs:39 IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(...)). appsettings.json:11 "Authority": "http://localhost:8180/realms/donhang".

refs simple.md:13 "applying the `[Authorize]` attribute to a ... controller, action ... limits access to that component to authenticated users"; JwtBearer is the only scheme (Program.cs@stage-2), so authenticated = valid token. OrdersController@stage-2: every action has [Authorize]/[Authorize(Policy="StaffOnly")]; ProductsController GET actions have none. configure-jwt-bearer-authentication.md:81 "If the request is not authorized, a 401 or 403 response is returned." output@stage-2 last line 401.

Keycloak docs (fetched): "the server is going to try to import any realm configuration file from the data/import directory"; containers: "the import directory is /opt/keycloak/data/import"; "If a realm already exists in the server, the import operation is skipped." DB guide: "By default, the server uses the dev-file database." docker-compose.yml@stage-2 mounts only the realm file into keycloak, no data volume, so dev-file data stays in the container.

outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/auth-and-orders.txt: "sign in as customer 1, at Keycloak (scripts/lib/keycloak.sh):" / "  got a token: eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs..." / two order lines with "customerId":1 / last line "401". scripts/lib/keycloak.sh sends password=donhang-dev-password only to Keycloak's login form. Script not re-run (stack not started); captured output used.

Follows from claims 4 and 6 as checked in the repo: at stage-2 the app has no password field and the API has no login endpoint, PasswordHasher or password_hash column, so neither process receives the password. RFC 6749 §1 names third-party apps storing credentials as the problem OAuth addresses.

Keycloak Server Admin Guide (fetched): "A realm manages a set of users, credentials, roles, and groups." "Realms are isolated from one another"; clients are "entities that can request Keycloak to authenticate a user". RFC 6749 §2: "Before initiating the protocol, the client registers with the authorization server." Run against the live stage-2 realm: token endpoint with client_id=not-registered -> {"error":"invalid_client"}; auth endpoint -> 400 "Client not found". Realm name "donhang" (donhang-realm.json:2).
